newsitem.title: USA: TECO planning Guatemala power plant.
newsitem.headline: TECO planning Guatemala power plant.

text.p: TECO Power Services said Thursday a partnership it has formed will build, own and operate a 120-megawatt pulverized coal power plant at Puerto Quetzal, Guatemala's principal Pacific Coast seaport.
The TECO Energy Inc subsidiary said the $170 million project is scheduled for completion by mid-1999.

It said the partnership was formed with a business interest in Guatemala and a U.S. based international power producer has signed a 15-year power supply agreement with Empresa Electrica de Guatemala SA, one of Guatemala's two principal electric utilities.
TECO said a consortium of J.A. Jones and Black and Veatch has been selected as the turnkey contractor.
The new plant will be located about 30 miles from Power Services' 78-megawatt Alborada Power Station, which went into service in September 1995.

The plant is the first coal-fired facility to be constructed in Central America and will use low-sulfur coal. As a result, it will more than meet current environmental standards which have been set by the World Bank.
TECO spokesman Mike Mahoney said the company will buy the coal on the open market.
The company noted "Annual load growth in Guatemala is averaging around nine percent and is likely to surge as the country's economy expands." -- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.
